finding.name: Version identity and point-in-time expression
finding.description: Separation of the abstract work from its dated expressions and rendered manifestations, and the identity of each version.

questions.text: How is the abstract statement distinguished from its dated versions and its rendered manifestations?
What version designator is assigned to each expression, and how is version ordering determined?
Which expression is the current consolidated one, and which are historical point-in-time versions?
What must change on the record whenever the content of an expression changes?

data_elements.name: work identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier of the abstract statement across all its versions.

data_elements.name: expression version designator
data_elements.description: Version label assigned to a dated expression of the statement.

data_elements.name: expression last-modified instant
data_elements.description: Instant at which the expression record last changed.

artifacts.name: Consolidated point-in-time expression
artifacts.description: A dated, citable rendering of the statement as it stood over a specific interval, produced by consolidating applied modifications.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative expression identifier from the publishing system of record; otherwise the governed work IRI plus the version designator; otherwise a UUID minted by the adopting Dimension with the fallback reason recorded.

finding.name: Issuing authority and mandate
finding.description: Which party issued the statement, under what legal or organisational competence, and by which recorded adoption decision.

questions.text: Which party issued the statement, and under what legal or organisational mandate?
Which body formally adopted the statement, and by which recorded decision?
Within what competence is the issuing authority empowered to bind?
What evidence supports the authority claim, and where does that evidence record live?

data_elements.name: issuing authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party record of the issuing authority.

data_elements.name: mandate basis reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the enabling instrument conferring authority to issue.

data_elements.name: adoption decision reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the record of the formal adoption or enactment decision.

finding.inline_only_rationale: Authority, mandate and adoption are carried as references to party records and decision records owned by other models; reproducing them here would duplicate externally owned evidence and drift toward owning an approval audit trail that this model explicitly disclaims.

finding.name: Constraint expression binding
finding.description: How each rule slot points at a constraint or rule expression owned by the referenced constraint model, and what binding metadata travels with the pointer.

questions.text: Which externally owned constraint or rule expression does each rule slot bind to?
At which binding point does the expression attach: rule condition, action refinement, or collection refinement?
Which expression language and version is the referenced constraint written in?
What happens to the statement when a referenced expression is unavailable or not understood?

data_elements.name: constraint expression reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to an expression record owned by the referenced constraint model.

data_elements.name: binding point code
data_elements.description: Where the referenced expression attaches within the rule slot.

data_elements.name: unresolved reference handling code
data_elements.description: Declared behaviour when a bound expression cannot be resolved or understood.

finding.inline_only_rationale: This finding deliberately carries only pointers and binding metadata. The constraint expression, its operators, operands and logical composition are owned by WM-KNW-013, so declaring an expression artifact here would reproduce a target model's content and violate the reference boundary.

finding.name: Combining and hit-policy declaration
finding.description: The strategy identifier the statement declares for reconciling multiple applicable rule slots, and where the normative definition of that strategy lives.

questions.text: Which combining or hit-policy strategy identifier does the statement declare for its rule slots?
Where is the normative definition of that strategy published, and who owns its execution?
Is the declared strategy order-sensitive, and if so what fixes the order?
Which conflict term applies when a permission and a prohibition both match?

data_elements.name: combining strategy identifier
data_elements.description: Declared identifier of the combining or hit-policy strategy.

data_elements.name: strategy definition reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the specification defining the declared strategy.

data_elements.name: conflict term code
data_elements.description: Declared policy-level conflict resolution term.

finding.inline_only_rationale: These are coded declarations pointing at strategies defined in external specifications. The evaluation that applies a combining algorithm or hit policy belongs to a referenced decision runtime, so this model produces no artifact and asserts no execution semantics here.

finding.name: Validity intervals and record time
finding.description: Distinct in-force, efficacy and applicability intervals, expressed as RFC 3339 instants, with event time kept separate from observation or ingestion time.

questions.text: When does the statement enter into force, and is that distinct from when it was adopted?
Over which interval is the statement efficacious, and can efficacy begin after entry into force?
To which facts or periods does the statement apply, as distinct from when it is in force?
What is the observation or ingestion instant at which each dated occurrence was captured in the register?
How is an instant with an unknown local offset represented without falsely asserting UTC local time?

data_elements.name: entry-into-force instant
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the statement enters into force.

data_elements.name: efficacy interval
data_elements.description: Start and end instants over which the statement is efficacious.

data_elements.name: applicability interval
data_elements.description: Period of facts to which the statement applies, which may precede entry into force.

data_elements.name: record ingestion time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the register captured the occurrence, distinct from event time.

finding.inline_only_rationale: Validity intervals and timestamps are scalar and interval values on the statement record; they are consumed by point-in-time resolution and carry no rendered form, so no artifact is declared and none is required to answer the questions.

finding.name: Record classification, access and retention
finding.description: How the statement record itself is classified and published, and how long its superseded expressions are retained before a declared disposition.

questions.text: What sensitivity classification applies to the statement record itself, as distinct from what it governs?
Which statements are published openly, and which are restricted to named audiences?
Which parts of a statement may be redacted while leaving it citable?
How long must superseded expressions be retained to support point-in-time reconstruction?
Which disposition action applies at the end of retention, who executes it, and what tombstone remains resolvable?

data_elements.name: record classification code
data_elements.description: Sensitivity classification of the statement record.

data_elements.name: publication audience code
data_elements.description: Declared audience for the published expression.

data_elements.name: retention period
data_elements.description: Minimum period for which superseded expressions must be retained.

data_elements.name: disposition action code
data_elements.description: Destruction, transfer or permanent preservation at end of retention.

data_elements.name: tombstone record
data_elements.description: Minimal resolvable record left after disposition of an expression.

finding.inline_only_rationale: Classification, audience, retention period, disposition class and tombstone are declarative fields on the statement record. Execution of destruction, transfer or preservation, and the log of that execution, belong to the adopting Dimension's records-retention authority, so no artifact is produced here.
